#95087. Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Massive Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Massive Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1362 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.
  • Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

Industry observers note that to use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Substantial Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches.

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season.

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

So why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic major boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the issues we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

It has been revealed that city had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

It has been revealed that iraola is aware of all this and said on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City.

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month.

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a significant game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’.

In a recent development, asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – noted: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’.

Sources indicate that in Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

It has been revealed that against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

In both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

Recent findings suggest that to take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's big boys.

In a recent development, and that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’.

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

Recent findings suggest that but Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Recent findings suggest that isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the big boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

‘I said at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’.

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Major Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

But a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put in one of their best performances under Ruben Amorim so far to sweep aside Frosinone at San Siro.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report by writing that Lazio, Roma and Juventus also had fun this weekend, scoring a flurry of goals in their victories, but it is Milan that might just come away from the round 12 feeling best.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Within 20 minutes, the Rossoneri had already blown the game wide open, eventually putting five past their opponents. All of them were spectacular, lightning-fast, and following the same pattern: every single one a counter-attack.

Industry observers note that it was a throwback style of football, yet infused with the visionary approach of Amorim, making it both fresh and truly beautiful to watch. There may not be official statistics on this, but conceding from five lethal transitions feels like a record as Frosinone’s strategy certainly went beyond mere self-sabotage.

Sources indicate that yet, on days like this, this Milan – an enigma to its opponents, with fluid movement and interchangeable positioning – are a truly daunting prospect. When Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Luka Modrić and others perform at such a high level, we see the potential of this side.

Industry observers note that the Diavolo have secured five wins in their last six league matches, yet in Europe, they have suffered three defeats in four games. Will Thursday’s clash against Olympiacos help restore the balance?

Recent findings suggest that there was nothing balanced about the game between Milan and Frosinone. It is true that Alvini’s incredibly bold (perhaps even reckless) side tried to go toe-to-toe with their opponents for an hour by attacking, playing long balls, and taking on defenders.

It has been revealed that yet, beyond this emphasis on a specific style of play, one could make more concrete assessments. The coach clearly understood how vital Raimondo is to a team featuring such direct and creative wingers, Ghedjemis on the right and Kvernadze (who was rather ineffective yesterday) on the left.

Raimondo was the perfect focal point for them and without him, things had already gone poorly against Cagliari. Alvini attempted to make adjustments but got it wrong: he abandoned his 4-2-3-1 formation in favour of a back three (Calvani, Monterisi, Cittadini).

Industry observers note that all this was undermined by a senseless tendency to push too high, maintaining a defensive line 57 metres from their own goal within a 3-4-3 setup that lacked a true striker, opting instead for a ‘false’ one in Schmid. Every time they lost possession, it resulted in a counter-attack and often a goal.

It might seem odd to start with Frosinone rather than the brilliance of Milan, but there’s no denying that the visitors played their part in the spectacle. This is a match that future opponents will need to study in minute detail, because Milan on the counter are a goal-scoring machine.

Amorim, too, has a knack for springing surprises, though as always the guessing game regarding his actual tactical setup for the day begins the moment the whistle blows. For example, it was not a back four as it appeared on paper.

Industry observers note that instead, the system actually gradually morphed into a 3-5-2, with Rabiot operating as a highly advanced right-sided central midfielder, almost an attacking midfielder. The key lies in the connection between the Frenchman and the stratospheric Moreira, who surged down the centre often.

Keeping everything running at full throttle was the incredible playmaking of Modrić, who also serves as the team’s primary ball-winner. So much for being a ‘pensioner’.

Milan proved flawless in exploiting both structural weaknesses and individual errors. Frosinone’s DNA is defined by a headlong, aggressive approach, but the opening goal – stemming from a sequence on the right flank involving Modrić and Rabiot – ended up as an own goal by Calvani.

Just four minutes in, and the match was effectively decided. While Frosinone usually thrive on quick, darting attacks, here the roles were reversed. Another full-pitch surge, initiated by Ramos winning the ball from Calvani and carried forward by Moreira and Rabiot, left the Portuguese player unmarked to make it 2-0.

Recent findings suggest that only a reckless back pass from Musah gifted Masini a goal to pull it back to 2-1. In the second half, however, Amorim addressed the one area that looked shaky: he withdrew Bartesaghi – who had been struggling against Ghedjemis – shifting Musah to full-back and pairing Jashari with Modrić.

According to recent reports, it paid off immediately: Jashari broke away and fired home the 3-1 following yet another rapid transition. And that wasn’t the only one: Pulisic surged clear on his own after a Frosinone corner (4-1), and Cissé, having just come on, joined the fray at full throttle to add the fifth (5-1).

Industry observers note that there were many top performances. Rabiot is like a freight train and deserved a goal. He had to settle for three assists (bringing his total to seven). Moreira is versatile, playing as a wing-back, a central midfielder, or a winger, much like he did for Belgium when they caused Italy so much trouble.

Ramos also moved well outside of his goal. Cissé was an absolute handful: he came on and scorrd, playing as a striker after the Portuguese felt a tweak. He did so with an effortless grace that makes him impossible for his markers to handle.

The end result is that Milan are back in fourth. The competition is fierce, but the Rossoneri are right there in the mix, and eventually, some of the others will stumble. Take Inter, for example. Frosinone need to rethink their strategy while waiting for the return of Raimondo.

They’ve overachieved so far, but now they might need to be a bit more prudent. And what about Milan? If they don’t turn their trip to Athens into a Greek tragedy, perhaps their European campaign can get back on track, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The stalemate made it eight points in four games in charge for Blackwell as Reds closed the gap on safety in League Two.

Reds had chances in the first half but second-placed Barnet put on the pressure in the second half but a mixture of solid defending and an inspired Vito Mannone kept the visitors at bay.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

“Wow, bloody hell, that was tough”, remarked Blackwell. "It's a very direct game, that's for sure, and they played it quite well, so I'm really pleased with the way the players dealt with it.

Sources indicate that “They're an experienced side and we had a lot of youngsters again today, so all credit to them. "I thought Ben Heneghan, once again, at the centre of the back three has done really well.

“It's a typical system to play against and I can see why they're high up in the league, it's causing teams problems. But I think overall, you know, Vito's not had many saves to make it, has he?.”.

Blackwell was pleased with how his reduced the amount of gilt-edged chances Dean Brennan’s side had. “There wasn't clear-cut chances,” he said. “It's a system that I've not seen for a long time, but it just meant we had to be focused all the time, they do things swiftly, they're long throws, long balls, the keeper kicks it from box to box.

In a recent development, “They know that the big nine is going to flick it on and they make runners in behind and your midfield and your centre-halves have to stay with runners. So it was a disciplined performance tonight against a team, like I say, who play a very direct style, but are good at what they do.”.

And the former Leeds boss highlighted that despite the gap in league positions, there was not much in quality between the two sides.

Recent findings suggest that blackwell said: “You look at it, it was top versus bottom, but you wouldn't have known. I don't think you'd have known.

It has been revealed that “Yes, they put us under a bit of pressure towards the end and exactly what a team at the top, full of confidence, you'd expect them to do that. But we were resilient and it's a difficult one for me to express the game other than it was concentration, do your job, throw your body in the way when required and stand up to a team that can bully you if you allow them to. Like I said, you know, Pemi [Aderoju] and Osman [Kamara] and Duke [Stephen Duke-McKenna, they've got a lot of youngsters we have and you're going to learn a lot from that.

Recent findings suggest that “I hope they learn a lot. But what I'm pleased about is the resilience.”.

And Blackwell added: “The question was about people coming to Crawley and getting easy points and I think we put a statement down certainly today that if you want to come to Crawley, you're going to have to earn your points if you want to work away with anything.

“So, once again, it's all credit to the players.”.

Former England forward Mark Hateley believes consistency is key for Leeds United defender Jayden Bogle as he targets a maiden Three Lions call-up.

He has gone from strength to strength in LS11, developing into one of Daniel Farke’s most trusted lieutenants.

Bogle has made no secret of his desire to break into the England squad, but faces stiff competition from high-profile stars.

“You just don't get into the England team now,” Hateley told The Yorkshire Post. “We have a lot of good players.

“You just have to look at the World Cup, some of the players that didn't go to the World Cup. We are where we are. We've got a Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane.

“You've probably got another two or three England players right now that could be Ballon d'Or winners in the next 5/10 years easily. That's the sort of opposition you've got trying to get into this England team. I'm not going to say team, I'm going to say squad.

It has been revealed that “Consistency will do the young man well. I think Jayden, he's put in his performances. He's of a good age. He's not that fully developed player, but he is playing well, consistently well. You put that together over another year or another season, you're 27, 28, then who knows?”.

Bogle was capped by England at under-20 level while on the books of Derby County and featured in the 2019 Toulon Tournament.

Two of his Leeds teammates - James Trafford and Dominic Calvert-Lewin - were named in Thomas Tuchel’s last England squad.

“A lot of opportunities can come your way,” said Hateley, who had a loan spell at Leeds in 1996. “Doors open.

It has been revealed that “When that door does open, you have to steam into that door. You can only do that by having that consistency.”.

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has insisted that struggling Brazilian superstar Vinicius Junior will "return to his full potential".

The 26-year-old signed a newly introduced mega-money deal with Real Madrid over the summer after rejecting the chance to make the move to Arsenal.

However, it has been a tough campaign for the attacker, who has only come up with one goal and three assists in 13 appearances for the club.

Vinicius was left out of the starting XI against Celta Vigo in the league on Saturday, instead featuring as a second-half substitute in his side's 2-1 success.

Mourinho has confirmed that the forward will be involved in Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven, and the Portuguese remains convinced that the South American will soon return to his highest level for Los Blancos.

Recent findings suggest that “He’ll return to his full potential. He’s young, and sometimes when players approach or pass the age of 30, they struggle to maintain their ideal physical condition and some lose a bit of their motivation," Mourinho told reporters during Monday's press conference.

According to recent reports, "Vini Jr. is young, and people can forget that he arrived very young and reached an extremely high level far too soon. He’s won everything, but when people were out to get him, he always noted he’s a really good lad and very empathetic towards everyone.

"That’s a fundamental foundation. He had a very positive impact the other day and I remember that against Villarreal he turned the game around, but he was out for four matches due to his sending-off and that disrupted his development and his confidence. At the weekend he came on well and helped turn the match around.

“He’s playing tomorrow and we’re all hoping to see him at his best. I saw him last season, but on the other side, with Benfica dominating and the Bernabeu silent. A goal from Vini Jr. and the tie was over.

Recent findings suggest that "That’s the Vini Jr. we want, but as far as I’m concerned there’s no pressure – he just needs to keep working hard as he’s been doing and help the team in attack and with defensive organisation. If he gives his all alongside me, he doesn’t need to be the man of the match.”.

Vinicius has been named in the squad for Real Madrid's European clash with PSV on Tuesday, but Endrick, Rodrygo, Raul Asencio and Ferland Mendy are out due to injuries.

Denzel Dumfries missed training on Monday and was regarded as a doubt, but the Netherlands international has been named in the squad.

Courtois, Lunin, Mestre; Militao, Huijsen, Trent, Konate, Cucurella, Carreras, Rudiger, Dumfries; Bellingham, Camavinga, Valverde, Tchouameni, Guler, Bernardo, Thiago; Vinicius, Mbappe, Espi, Brahim, Diomande.

However, they have yet to share the pitch: Tzimas was substituted in the 77th minute and Kostoulas came on a minute later.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has been encouraged by Tzimas' return to first-team training, but is keen not to rush him back.

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 18:19, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 18:21.

Manchester United are reportedly in the mix to sign Al-Ahli centre-forward Ivan Toney when the January transfer window opens for business.

Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury problems have left the Red Devils dangerously short in the final third of the field, and the expectation is that the club will make a centre-forward signing when the winter market opens at the start of 2027.

Man United have been linked with a move for Toney of late, with the England international believed to be keen to return to the Premier League.

According to TEAMtalk, the 20-time English champions are being 'kept informed' of the developments surrounding the 30-year-old.

The report claims that a number of clubs are considering moves for Toney; a loan deal with an option to buy is believed to be a possibility in January.

Toney is allegedly still hopeful that he can be in contention for a spot in the England squad for Euro 2028 and believes that his best chance of that occurring would be to prove that he can still find the back of the net in the Premier League.

Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur are also believed to be monitoring the situation, with Toney not short of interest.

The striker scored 72 goals and registered 23 assists in 141 appearances for Brentford between 2020 and 2024 before making the move to Al-Ahli.

Toney has a record of 88 goals and 21 assists in 110 appearances for Al-Ahli, including 16 goals and four assists in 17 outings in all competitions this term.

There is no question that Man United need to bring in a forward in January, especially with Joshua Zirkzee potentially moving on at the start of 2027.

Man United need a player who is proven in the Premier League and one who can have an immediate impact - Toney fits that brief.

The striker has scored 36 goals and registered 11 assists in 85 appearances in the Premier League, and he has the personality required to represent a club of Man United's ilk.

The Red Devils would also not have to break the bank to sign Toney, with a loan deal a very attractive proposition, and Mauricio Pochettino's side should not pass up the chance to do what could be a very successful piece of January business.

Alphadjo Cisse has revealed that he would like to add more assists to his game, as well as why he has Matteo Gabbia to thank above all.

In a recent development, milan put on a ruthless display at San Siro on Sunday night, beating Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four. Calvani’s own-goal started the rout, while Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari and Christian Pulisic all scored.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Cisse got his name on the scoresheet again just minutes after coming on, netting his ninth goal of the season. Diego Moreira set him up with a nice through ball in transition, and though the offside flag went up initially, VAR overturned it to award the goal.

After the game, Cisse spoke to both Sky and DAZN to give his thoughts on what was another very positive night for him personally and for the team. His comments are via MilanNews.

What position do you prefer to play?

Industry observers note that “I definitely always try to contribute in all positions, and I definitely prefer to play in my own position, but I’m always available in all roles. Which position? I won’t say (laughs).”.

Where can you still grow and what does Amorim ask of you?

It has been revealed that “I have to improve in many other areas. As always, scoring is always great. I’d also like to add a few assists for some of my team-mates, but the most key thing was always to bring home three points, and today we did that.”.

Is there a team-mate you have to thank in particular?

“I definitely think Gabbia, because I was initially coming from Serie B, and settling into that kind of environment is never easy. But I had teammates who welcomed me very well, him especially, so for me everything was much easier.”.

We also see you as a possible centre-forward….

“I’ll tell you the truth, come on, I’ll tell you. I prefer to play in the attacking midfield because, as I’ve always done, I always want to try to make plays, to entertain people. But maybe, who knows, I’ll also play as a striker, I don’t know. Let’s see…”.

Did you know you weren’t offside?

“At first I thought it was. Then, as they were checking it a bit, I thought it wasn’t.”.

It has been revealed that you’re Milan’s top scorer. Will we see a bicycle kick soon?

In a recent development, “The overhead kick used to be my specialty, but now it’s not. Let’s hope it happens. It’s always a great feeling to score, I want to add a few assists too. The vital thing was the three points, and we got them.”.

How far along are you in your development?

“Right now, I’m not even halfway there. Maybe even lower. There’s still a lot of work to do to get there. But I’m in the right place, and hopefully we can get there.”.

Have you ever thought about what would have happened if you had gone to PSV?

“Better not to think about it. Let’s just say that I’ve always made the right decisions with my family, and thanks go to them, to the coach, to my team-mates, and I’m in the right place and on the right path.”.

How much is Amorim protecting you?

“Progress is the right word, because we’ve changed coaches, and it’s never easy. We’re a great team, with many champions. We still have a lot of work to do. Milan always has our backs, and that’s very important to me.”.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 05:59 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:11 EST, 23 November 2026.

Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapsed during a live interview immediately after winning a trophy with his Boca Juniors side.

The 32-year-old was one of the focal points of a World Cup side that reached the final last summer, and went on to win the Copa Sudamericana on Saturday evening after beating Brazil's Atletico Mineiro 2-0 in Barranquilla.

But amid the thick humidity and Colombian heat, Paredes became overwhelmed moments after lifting the trophy.

After giving a brief interview, Paredes was captured closing his eyes, before falling towards the interviewer, who attempted to break his fall.

Instead, the former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder hit the ground, with attendants rushing to help him after his collapse.

Paredes had been taken off in the second-half after suffering from heat-related dizziness, with humidity at 80 per cent heading into the match, and 32-degree-temperatures.

Leandro Parades collapsed to the floor during a post-match interview after winning the Copa Sudamericana with Boca Juniors.

The interviewer attempted to break his fall as the former PSG crumpled to the turf.

Industry observers note that 'He felt dizzy towards the end of the first-half,' his manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena explained of the substitution. 'He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second-half, you could see he was struggling.'.

Fortunately, Paredes was revived quickly and treated in the treatment room, before re-joining his team's celebrations after claiming the South American trophy.

The star shared a brief statement on social media confirming he was fine after the interview aired.

'We're fine,' Paredes confirmed with a picture taken during treatment, before adding in a separate caption: 'Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just a dizziness from so many turns together'.

Paredes' triumph for his club side comes months after agonising defeat to Spain in New York at the World Cup final in July.

Argentina were felled by a solitary goal from Ferran Torres to end their reign as world champions, before the match descended into petty scraps - with Paredes at the heart of the bad behaviour.

Paredes furiously shoved Spain substitute Gavi to the floor after the final whistle blew, earning himself a punchy 10-match suspension from FIFA.

He faced three assault charges, while teammate Nahuel Molina faced two, and both players were also fined $90,000 (£66,000).

Paredes himself admitted that the length of the ban had put his international future under consideration.

Industry observers note that 'It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,' Paredes told the media in September. 'Because of the suspension as well, because of (Lionel Messi) Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

'I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make.'.

Paredes' announcement came just days after Messi decided to hang up his international boots, with the talismanic Argentina superstar treated to a magnificent send-off during the early Autumn international break.

'Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled,' Paredes added.

Paredes updated fans after the incident to confirm he was okay before rejoining the festivities with his team-mates (Source: Instagram/Leandro Parades).

'We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us.'.

Although unable to compete alongside him in their country's colours for one last time, Paredes joined Messi on the pitch in Buenos Aires for his final farewell, and shared an emotional tribute post to his former captain.

'THANK YOU FOR ABSOLUTELY EVERYTHING CAPTAIN,' he captioned a carousel of photos of himself and Messi.

'It was a dream to be able to have achieved everything we achieved together and to have defended this shirt and our country with you, I'm leaving and we'll miss you always.

'It was a pleasure to be one of your soldiers for all these years and I will be forever! I love you buddy.'.

Not that his initial few months in West Yorkshire were particularly easy.

January moves are often not straightforward and so it proved for the left-sided player.

He joined a Town side wrestling with form concerns - a few hours after he made his debut, Lee Grant was sacked - and the mood in the stands hardly improved as winter turned to spring.

Thankfully, the mood music is transformed these days at second-placed Town, who visit Doncaster Rovers in a Yorkshire derby on Thursday evening.

Mumba, whose partner had a baby earlier this year, said: "My family have all settled. My missus, the kids, my daughters, they're all good.

"I've settled. This is home. Obviously, it's not far from where my actual family live, which is up north in Newcastle.

"Everything now, for me, is where I need it to be. I'm exactly where I feel like I'm meant to be at this point in my career.

"I think I was closer to France when I was at Plymouth than actually to my family up north!. I've been all over the place. I started off at Sunderland and went to Norwich, Peterborough and Plymouth.

"It's been quite a journey, to be fair. It's finally good to be in the middle, at the centre of everything and have the support that I have closer to me and around me.

"I also had pre-season to help me find my focus and concentration and really start again and start reaping the rewards.".

Mumba is starting to display the form which convinced Town to shelve out a significant fee of around £1million to bring him back north in the January window.

A fan favourite during his time at Home Park, Mumba played a major part in Argyle's League One title-winning campaign in 2022-23.

Highlights included a superb solo goal in the Devonians' first game back in the second-tier after a 13-year absence in August 2023 - ironically against Town.

Mumba, who signed a long-term deal with Town until at least 2029, is now chasing a second promotion from the third tier - in the blue and white of Town as opposed to the green and white of Argyle.

He continued: "Right now, I would say I'm getting that vibe that I got from Plymouth. For me, it's the dressing room, players and togetherness that gives you the success.

Recent findings suggest that "At Norwich, it was the same. The year we got promoted at (Plymouth), I feel like that togetherness was really what was behind the success, what a lot of people don't see. Come Saturday, you're going to war with your mate.

According to recent reports, "Whoever's next to you, you're going into the battle. You've got to have that relationship and you've got to care for each other.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

According to recent reports, city will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

In a recent development, could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

It has been revealed that in the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz.

Industry observers note that it could have been a hat-trick. It could even have been four as Haaland, taking the captain’s armband as Rúben Dias was withdrawn during the interval, clipped the top of the crossbar with a header and then was denied by goalkeeper Matvei Safonov as the striker slid in.

In a recent development, “Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis [Enrique, PSG’s coach] said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky,” Maresca claimed before being asked whether he would relish facing PSG again, later in this competition. “My feeling is we are there. We are close,” he added.

Did City deserve a draw? No one was predicting that at half-time as they were suffering as comprehensive a defeat as was inflicted by the commission. Accused of “sham” contracts to inflate income, this was a sham of a performance, made all the more emphatic because of how brilliant PSG, and their exceptional 21-year-old winger Désiré Doué, were.

Désiré Doué with a brilliant finish from range to give PSG an early lead in Manchester 😮‍💨 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/Uwilx7I37H.

There is a certain irony that it was PSG who inflicted this defeat, ending City’s run of eight wins from eight in all competitions under Maresca.

In a recent development, it was a meeting of two clubs empowered more than any other by the riches of Gulf states: Abu Dhabi versus Qatar. Both have also had their run-ins over money. Both were sanctioned, but escaped full bans by Uefa for breaching financial fair play rules.

The question, also, was: would the eighth meeting of these clubs in the Champions League in the last 11 seasons be the last for some time?

So we should savour it and we did. That included Pep Guardiola on his first return to the Etihad – in a sign of solidarity – after quitting at the end of last season. Not that he savoured much of what he saw as PSG dominated City to such an extent that their fans adopted the “Poznan” celebration and the home supporters were silenced.

City could have gone in front before they conceded with the erratic Safonov – who was Gianluigi Donnarumma’s understudy and has become his unlikely replacement – punching a corner against his own crossbar before Antoine Semenyo shot the rebound over.

In a recent development, then PSG ran all over City. They broke far too easily and scored far too easily. Not once, but twice, to go 2-0 up.

For the first, PSG countered, with City struggling to cover, and Doué caught out Donnarumma with a low shot inside his right-hand post from 22 yards.

Then PSG sliced through City’s defence with Ousmane Dembélé scooping the ball across the area to Doué who returned it back. Dembélé stooped to head home.

Ousmane Dembélé doubles PSG's lead just 2 minutes after they scored the first 🤯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/MxhJ3oCWpC.

Enzo Fernández should have scored from a close-range header and Haaland did, glancing in an inswinging Ndiaye cross.

In a recent development, finally the City fans found their voices but then they were silenced. What a calamity for Donnarumma as he got a hand to Akliouche’s shot on the turn, but only palmed the ball up in the air before it bounced into the net.

But City did not stop. Nuno Mendes headed Josko Gvardiol’s flick off the line, Fernández hit a post before Bouaddi set up Haaland and he swept the ball past Safonov.

In a recent development, I think our start was quite good until the first goal. Then we conceded the second after one [more] minute and that created bad feelings so we struggled.

Second half we were much, much, much better and we probably deserved even something more.

It was strange to be honest because until the first goal we were in the game. We created things, didn’t concede and then the first goal led to the second one. When you concede two goals in two minutes it could [get] even worse.

According to recent reports, at half-time we adjust something, didn’t lose our balance and in the second half we created enough to deserve something more. We adjusted the way we were pressing, something on the ball [too].

[A message for the fans?] We feel sorry for the first half but I think we’re quite happy now. Significant game on Saturday [Ipswich at home at 3pm].

When Manchester City endured their first major sanction over financial fair play in 2014, the biggest club accused alongside them that summer were Paris St-Germain, another Champions League arriviste who had been raised from mediocrity to the elite by some frantic spending from a Middle East fossil fuel dynasty.

Then, 12 years ago, both sides bitterly opposed the Uefa sanctions imposed on them – although they eventually agreed to the terms. Now, they face one another in Manchester with PSG aiming for a third consecutive Champions League title, and City fighting for their lives in the face of an overwhelming guilty verdict for nine years of Premier League rule-breaking.

Recent findings suggest that both clubs are transformed from the entities that their current owners acquired. While PSG now find themselves at the centre of the new order in European football, City are once again on the outside.

According to recent reports, whatever the outcome of this process, I won’t forget the connection and relationships I had here. It will never be erased.

Good evening, and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Manchester City and Paris St-Germain, champions in 2025 and 2026 and favourites to become only the fourth club, after Real Madrid (who have done it twice), Ajax and Bayern Munich to win a hat-trick of European Cups.

Industry observers note that after Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has mentioned he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the complications addressed.

Having stated that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. But I don’t think it would serve anyone to take the stance during the live coverage that anything that is happening on the field is unimportant, redundant and ultimately void because of the guilty verdicts, and hence adopt a flippant tone. I propose once the match starts to treat it as a match while not ignoring the context.

Right, let’s get stuck into the Gulf State sovereign wealth fund derby… sorry, imposible to resist.

PSG have made a slow start to their Ligue 1 campaign, their worst since Luis Enrique’s first season in charge. Starting with two draws and a defeat, they have rallied with three successive victories to climb up to sixth as the head coach, as he tends to do in the league, rotates his midfielders and forwards like crazy, to whose ranks he has added the World Cup-winner Ferran Torres. The summer signing scored a hat-trick in his Champions League debut for the club, a 6-1 mauling of Slovan Bratislava.

City, too, started their European campaign with a win, Erling Haaland scoring both goals in the 2-0 victory over Porto at the Dragao and you won’t need me to remind you that they have won all six of their Premier League games to lead Arsenal by three points at the top of the table.

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 18:38, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 18:41.

Manchester United are reportedly planning to make a move for Villarreal defender Alex Freeman when the January transfer window opens for business.

The Red Devils have conceded 34 times across all competitions this season, which is the worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues.

Man United are expected to be busy during the winter market, with at least one defender likely to arrive, while the club are also remarked to be planning to sign a striker.

Centre-back has been a major problem for the 20-time English champions this season, but right-back is also an issue, with Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui having tough campaigns.

According to Football Insider, Man United are planning to bring a newly introduced right-back to Old Trafford in January in the shape of Villarreal's Freeman.

The report claims that Man United scouts have been impressed by Freeman's level since he made the move to European football with Villarreal.

Freeman is well-known to fresh Red Devils head coach Mauricio Pochettino following their time together with the USA; the 22-year-old has 28 caps for his national team, scoring three goals and registering three assists in the process.

"There will be players in that US national team that Pochettino will be a big fan of," journalist Pete O'Rourke stated on the Transfer Insider podcast.

"If he feels any player from that squad that can come in and improve the Manchester United side, then that is something he'd be foolish not to look at as well.

"There's been talk of Alex Freeman the full-back from Villarreal as being a potential target, after he has been outstanding playing in Spain.

"Obviously defence is going to be a top priority for United over the next couple of transfer windows to try and reshape the squad, and Pochettino could be key to that deal.".

Freeman started his professional career with Orlando City, making 42 appearances for the club, scoring six goals and registering seven assists, ahead of a move to Villarreal in January 2026.

The defender has one goal in 26 appearances for Villarreal, including four outings in the Champions League, while he has netted once in 17 appearances for the Yellow Submarine this season.

Freeman has a contract with Villarreal until the summer of 2032.

Signed on an initial loan deal until January from Championship club Lincoln City, Collins' long road back to first-team duty—after sustaining a serious knee injury at his parent club almost exactly 12 months ago—meant Rovers had to be patient regarding his availability.

The debut display of the senior striker, who turns 36 on December 1, when he came off the bench midway through the second half in Saturday's draw at Yorkshire rivals Bradford City, also preceded a bit of chatter among Rovers followers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Collins indicated what he was all about, demonstrating his nous to set up Rovers' first equaliser - a brilliant overhead kick from Jordan Thomas - and leading the line in canny fashion.

Given the summer departure of Billy Sharp – a player who similarly brought leadership and nous to the table in the final third – Collins will fill a void in that regard.

The former Republic of Ireland forward has been promoted seven times in his career from the lower leagues with five different clubs – Lincoln, Derby County, Shrewsbury Town, Northampton Town and Luton Town.

There was plenty of noise in the build-up to Saturday from Collins too.

Rovers chief Grant McCann revealed: "We've just lacked a little bit of character at times. He's certainly not been quiet on the training ground.

"You can certainly hear the noise levels lift. We did a session (on Friday) on the training pitch and had an 11 v 11 game and Collo was in the team that we were preparing against and he scored against us. And we were like: 'here we go'.

Sources indicate that "I could feel the group going a wee bit quiet when we conceded the first goal (at Bradford) and Collo just picked them up and went: ''Lads. I've done this against loads of clubs, so don't be worried'.".

Another welcome returnee was experienced Matty Pearson, who cast aside a booking in the first 25 seconds to stay on message at Valley Parade in only his second league outing of the campaign following injury.

Rovers host Pearson's former club Huddersfield Town on Thursday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Several AC Milan players have been highly praised by the Italian media after the 5-1 dismantling of Frosinone at San Siro.

It has been revealed that milan ended up with goals from five different sources as Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted, in addition to the opening goal which was an own-goal by Calvani. Adrien Rabiot got three assists, while Diego Moreira shone too.

It was a statement result and a ruthless display of the weapons that the Rossoneri have in transition, and it moves Ruben Amorim’s side back into the top four, while they remain five points off leaders Lazio.

Starting with La Gazzetta dello Sport, they gave the team’s overall performance a score of 8 out of 10, which is the same mark that they gave Amorim for his selections and tactical handling of what could have been a tough game on paper.

Rabiot was the Serie A Man of the Match and he gets the crown from La Gazzetta too, scoring an 8. The worst performer was Davide Bartesaghi, who struggled in his battle with Ghedjemis and got a 5.5.

Moreira matched Rabiot with an 8, while Pulisic and Luka Modric were given a 7.5. Four players scored a 7: Yunus Musah, Ramos, Jashari and Cisse. Sankhoun Diawara (6.5) passed the test, with Koni De Winter, Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan being given a 6.

Corriere dello Sport were a tad harsher with their scoring, giving Rabiot a 7.5 as the highest score. Jashari, Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and Ramos were handed a 7. They gave Cisse a 6.5, and everyone else got a passing score. Amorim (7.5) was also praised.

Tuttosport meanwhile gave Rabiot an 8, distributing 7.5s instead to Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and the coach Amorim. Scores of 7 went to Jashari, Musah, Ramos and Cisse. Gila, De Winter and Diawara got given a 6.5, and everyone else a 6.

#95047. Breaking: Gary Neville tears into Man United's Matthijs de Ligt for 'unforgivable' defending that led to Leny Yoro's red card - and claims duo played like 'they have never had basic defensive training'

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (775 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Gary Neville tears into Man United's Matthijs de Ligt for 'unforgivable' defending that led to Leny Yoro's red card - and claims duo played like 'they have never had basic defensive training'

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.
  • After just eight minutes, his prepares were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.

After just eight minutes, his prepares were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.

A long ball from Ronald Araujo should have been dealt with easily by De Ligt, but the Dutchman found himself in no man's land, left the ball, and Alexander Isak raced clear.

That left Yoro scrambling to try to recover the situation for his side, but Isak stepped across him and he ended up fouling the Reds forward.

Referee Sam Barrott wasted no time in pulling out the red card, and United found themselves reduced to 10 men just minutes into a vital clash.

And former United defender Neville didn't hold back when it came to his analysis as he tore into the two players at fault.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

Gary Neville torn into Manchester United duo Leny Yoro (right) and Matthijs de Ligt after the former was sent off.

Neville (pictured) questioned why the duo were playing as if they had 'never had basic training of how to play in defence'.

It has been revealed that 'When I saw De Ligt's name on the team sheet I have to admit I was absolutely stunned,' he mentioned, speaking on Sky Sports. 'And the reason I was stunned was because of this. If you'd watched him in Como four weeks ago he was very much well off it and that is just a basic ball over the top.

'It's his problem to start with, Yoro can be further across, but De Ligt is miles away from it, then Yoro has to get further round, he reacts late, his anticipation is poor. It's so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these types of mistakes.

'You could argue Isak delays to make sure Yoro runs into him, but it's naivety.'.

Pochettino was left scrambling to think of ideas to tighten up the defence but, before he could bring Harry Maguire on, it was 2-0 through Florian Wirtz.

Maguire eventually came on but it felt like too little, too late.

'We saw him in Como and he has been out for a year,' Neville continued on De Ligt. 'It is really tough to come back. To have him out there in a game like this, he has been exposed. Yoro's positioning is poor, he has to be across, you have to cover your mate. It is bad all around from United.

'Michael Carrick will be watching and say that's what I was having to deal with.'.

Recent findings suggest that and his criticism didn't stop there. After having the chance to re-watch the incident, Neville's criticism grew even stronger.

De Ligt (left) failed to deal with a long ball as Alexander Isak (right) raced away before the foul.

Former United captain Roy Keane (pictured) added that he was 'amazed' by the errors made.

'It's as bad defending from two centre backs defending a long ball as you will see,' the former defender, who likened a return from a year out to playing after six pints of alcohol, added. 'De Ligt is well out of it - he's been out so I have some sympathy. But between them, to let the ball beat you, it's unforgivable.

Industry observers note that 'It is shocking. Whilst Man United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping a clean sheet.

'It's basic understanding of how to play a position. It's the fundamentals. It's like these guys have never had basic training of how to play in defence.'.

Former United captain Roy Keane chimed in too, adding at half-time: 'It doesn't matter if it's a back four or back five, you do the basics right.

In a recent development, 'I'm amazed at this level, I know he's been out a while, but it's really poor defending. He's never getting that ball.

'If you're a defender you always expect the worst. Isak's done well and I actually don't think he's going to get the ball.

Sources indicate that 'There's no way he's (Yoro) getting the ball, it's clumsy by United. Straight ball over the top and he's in big trouble. But there's no way he's getting that ball. I know he's quick and sharp but it's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Atletico Madrid will be bidding to return to winning ways in the Champions League when they continue their league stage campaign against Viking FK on Wednesday night.
  • This match will represent the first-ever contest between Atletico and Viking, although the Spanish team have won six of their seven previous meetings against Norwegian clubs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 19:14, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:42.

Atletico Madrid will be bidding to return to winning ways in the Champions League when they continue their league stage campaign against Viking FK on Wednesday night.

This match will represent the first-ever contest between Atletico and Viking, although the Spanish team have won six of their seven previous meetings against Norwegian clubs.

Atletico boast a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's Champions League league stage, with the result leaving them 23rd in the overall table on four points.

Diego Simeone's side opened their league stage campaign with a 2-1 defeat to Liverpool before beating Manchester United and then drawing with Stuttgart, but they suffered a 2-0 home defeat to Bayern Munich in their last fixture in the competition.

Atletico have European games against PSV Eindhoven, Bodo/Glimt and Fenerbahce to come after this one, and it would be a major shock if they were not present in the knockout round of the tournament.

The Red and Whites will enter this match off the back of a 3-0 win over Getafe in Spain's top flight, with the result leaving them third in the La Liga table on 31 points, five points behind leaders Barcelona.

Atletico lost 2-1 on aggregate to Arsenal in last season's Champions League semi-finals, and they have been runners-up in this tournament on two occasions (2014 and 2016).

Viking, meanwhile, have a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's league stage, and they actually sit above Atletico in the table (22nd).

The Eliteserien champions lost their section opener to Stuttgart before claiming a point in a 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich, but they were then beaten by Aston Villa at Villa Park.

The Dark Blues did have a huge European win last time out, though, recording a 4-1 victory over Sabah, which gave their hopes of qualification a huge boost.

Viking, who are jointly-managed by Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim and Morten Jensen, are playing in the Champions League for the first time since 1992-93, when they were beaten by Barcelona in the first round.

The Norwegian outfit have scored in their last 12 European matches, which is a club record, while none of Atletico's last 42 Champions League fixtures have finished goalless.

Atletico will be without the services of Ademola Lookman (knee), Marc Pubill (ankle) and Cristian Romero (muscular) for the Champions League fixture with Viking.

Lee Kang-in could be introduced into the starting side on Wednesday, with the 25-year-old potentially featuring alongside Julian Alvarez in the final third of the field.

Alex Baena is set to continue down the left off the back of his excellent performance against Getafe, while Johnny Cardoso is likely to feature in the middle of the midfield.

As for Viking, Anders Baertelsen (foot), Sondre Bjorshol (knee), Nick D'Agostino (leg) and Martin Ove Roseth (muscular) are out of the match due to injury problems.

Meanwhile, Veton Berisha (unspecified) and Kristoffer Haugen (unspecified) both need to be assessed before final decisions on their availability can be made.

Peter Christiansen is the team's leading goalscorer this season with 19, and the 26-year-old will once again feature in the final third of the field.

Atletico Madrid possible starting lineup:.

Oblak; Llorente, Le Normand, Hancko, Grimaldo; Simeone, Barrios, Cardoso, Baena; Kang-in, Alvarez.

Viking FK possible starting lineup:.

Ostbo; Heggheim, Stensness, Falchener, Auklend; Bjordal, Bell, Askildsen; Christiansen, Botheim, Tripic.

Viking have enough quality to find the back of the net against Atletico, but we are fully expecting Simeone's side to secure a valuable three points in the Champions League.

EFL cult hero Paul Mullin on his Bradford City mistake and how Rotherham United can turn a corner

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (928 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mullin joined the Bantams on loan from Wrexham in the second half of last season try to push them over the line to promotion but it did not work out as planned for him.
  • The striker started just two League One games and failed to find the net as Bradford reached the play-offs, but lost in the semi-finals to Bolton Wanderers.
  • Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mullin joined the Bantams on loan from Wrexham in the second half of last season try to push them over the line to promotion but it did not work out as planned for him.

The striker started just two League One games and failed to find the net as Bradford reached the play-offs, but lost in the semi-finals to Bolton Wanderers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Industry observers note that his next loan, to Rotherham, has been much better for him personally, with eight goals so far, but less so the Millers, who are in the League Two relegation zone after 15 matches. Changing the second half of the equation is about cutting out the mistakes which have bedevilled the team, and 32-year-old Mullin claims he has a substantial part to play in that.

"I'm really enjoying it," states Mullin of his time in South Yorkshire.

Industry observers note that "I love working with the manager (Alex Bruce) and the players every single day. It's a nice place to be, but t could be a hell of a lot better. We've had so much bad luck this season.

"It's been unfortunate, as well as bad performances at times.

"Within those games we haven't won, we've probably played very, very well for 30 minutes, 40 minutes, even 60 minutes. There's been a ten-minute patch where something happened and we just couldn't seem to get the game back.

Recent findings suggest that "That's sort of been the story of our season – silly mistakes that could easily be cut out. It's things that you wouldn't expect people to make.

"Everybody has periods throughout the season where they struggle to get results.

"I know it's the start of the season, but hopefully that can be ours and it flips on its head for the rest of the season, I've got full belief we can.”.

It is perhaps no coincidence Rotherham are so error-prone when one looks at their age profile.

In a recent development, "We've got a lot of young lads in the changing room,” he noted. “People don't realise when you're playing, everybody looks the same age.

Industry observers note that "When you're young, you do make naive mistakes. You make a mistake trying to do the right thing. You're not trying to make the mistake, you're trying to do the right thing.

"As you go through men's football, you need to realise quickly there's consequences to little mistakes and they can affect the results of a game, which in turn, if they carry on, can affect the rest of a career.

"It's something you need to figure out quite swiftly.

"I think we're getting better at that as time goes by and we are getting closer to where we want to be.

"We're still nowhere near, but we're getting closer. Hopefully we can build on it and I've no doubt that come the end of the season, it will look a hell of a lot different.

It has been revealed that "We've probably got four players, maybe, over the age of 30 and the rest are probably under 26, so there's not really much middle ground. I suppose that's part and parcel of football.

According to recent reports, "At Wrexham I went from middle-of-the-road to being one of the experienced ones and then Bradford was a very experienced group when I got there. It's different clubs, different scenarios and I understand why.

"As experienced players, it's up to us to try to give them as much as we can to progress and to give them the best chance of having a great career. We've got some really, really talented players and I'm looking forward to seeing how they progress.

"If we can cut out the mistakes – which aren't anything to do with tactics – and we can help each other out a little bit more in that aspect, I think we'll be fine and we will see us start to climb the table.".

A key figure and cult hero in Wrexham's rise up the division, Mullin found himself marginalised in the Championship.

He was one of three forwards signed by Bradford in January, along with Ethan Wheatley and Kayden Jackson.

"Bradford was just the complete opposite of what I was told it was going to be," he noted. "It's fair enough. The team was doing really well.

"I was told they were going to change to be a certain way I'd fit in.

"When I got there, the manager (Graham Alexander) decided otherwise. That's his job.

"He had the team at the top end of the table, so I understand why. But equally, if it was explained that way to me before I went, then I probably wouldn't have done it.

Sources indicate that "It was unfortunate, but it's never bothered me. It's how you're treated which is important to me and the manager was respectful about it.

"He explained that he didn't want to change any more. He basically had played that way all season, and he had a change of heart and wanted to stick with it. That's fine.".

Mullin, whose son Albi is autistic, was speaking at an event to promote the EFL's Power of 72 campaign celebrating the impact of club charities.

The striker joined an adult football session for people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), at Parkgate Astro in Rotherham.

He has repeatedly been linked with Premier League clubs and a recent report credited the likes of Newcastle United and Sunderland with interest.

Deane, who made 171 appearances across three spells at Bramall Lane, does not want to see Peck depart.

Industry observers note that he told The Yorkshire Post via BetWright.com: “I'd be very surprised if he left. The club has had a really turbulent time in the transfer market in the summer. Obviously, with no parachute payments coming in now, you have to think, what signal does that send to the fans, to the club and to everybody else in the division?

“They have to show some ambition. I think, from the manager's point of view, it'd be a devastating blow if the club were in a position or wanted to be in a position to sell him. The other thing is, from the kid's development, I think it's very key to solidify himself at the level and then look to use that as a foundation.

“If he is going to end up in the Premier League, you have to have a ground in somewhere. Sheffield United is, for me, one of the best clubs in the Championship at the moment, he probably couldn't wish to be at a better club.”.

Sheffield United would like to tie Peck down to a new contract, although it may prove difficult to retain the England youth international if the vultures circle.

In a recent interview, Blades boss Chris Wilder stated: “We talked about extending the contracts of the young players and Sydie's one of those players that we'd love to have that discussion with.

“If anything comes up that you can't turn down, I don't think anybody would turn that down. I've stated it all along, you're not just turning that from a club's point of view, you're turning that down from an opportunity for the player to go and play in the Premier League. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 23 Nov 2026 19:39, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 19:39.

Hibernian FC host Dundee FC in the Scottish Premiership at Easter Road Stadium on Tuesday.

The fixture was moved from October 31 because of Hibernian's Premier Sports Cup semi-final, and both clubs arrive after heavy defeats on November 21, with Hibernian beaten 4-0 at home by Dundee United and Dundee thrashed 8-0 by Heart of Midlothian at Dens Park.

Marink Reedijk's Hibernian sit 11th in the Scottish Premiership table with 11 points from 13 games, a return of three wins, two draws and eight defeats, and their goal difference of minus six is the product of 15 goals scored and 21 conceded.

The Hibees are the only club in the division yet to win a league match at home this season, and they have conceded 15 goals in seven league games at Easter Road.

Dundee United made that record worse on Saturday, with Zac Sapsford scoring from the rebound after Raphael Sallinger saved his sixth-minute penalty, adding a second before half time, and Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall completing a 4-0 win that was Hibernian's heaviest home defeat to United.

Reedijk was appointed on September 24 after David Gray was sacked, and he lost his first three league games in charge, 1-0 at Dundee United on October 10 and 2-1 at home to both Falkirk on October 17 and Celtic on October 25.

The cup has been kinder, as goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath beat Heart of Midlothian 2-1 at Hampden Park on November 1, Hibernian's first win over their city rivals at the national stadium after four defeats there, and set up a Premier Sports Cup final against Rangers on Sunday, December 13.

McGrath then struck a 25-yard shot just before the hour at Pittodrie on November 7, and substitutes Callum Wright, Nicky Cadden and Thibault Klidje added the rest in a 4-0 win that was Hibernian's biggest at Aberdeen since 1968 and remains Reedijk's only league victory.

Joe Newell, who wore the captain's armband against United in place of the injured Felix Passlack, spoke afterwards of the players' shame and embarrassment, and the midfielder will know that Tuesday offers the first chance to answer it in front of the Easter Road crowd.

Steven Pressley's Dundee sit seventh with 17 points from 13 games, a record of five wins, two draws and six defeats that leaves them six points and four places above Hibernian, with 18 goals scored and 23 conceded.

The Dee had conceded only 15 times in their first 12 league games and collected five wins in that run, with Owen Goodman playing every minute in goal and keeping two clean sheets.

That solidity vanished on Saturday, when Hearts led 4-0 at half time and Owen Bevan was sent off on 56 minutes for a foul on Claudio Braga, with the visitors winning 8-0 in what The Courier described as Dundee's worst-ever defeat at Dens Park.

Pressley took responsibility for the display afterwards, while pundit Richard Foster argued the players must also own a result that was Hearts' biggest top-flight win since 1957.

The defeat came a fortnight after a 2-1 loss at St Johnstone on November 7, and it ended an unbeaten home run of four league games for a side that had collected the bulk of its points at Dens Park.

Dundee will also remember that Hibernian won the first meeting 2-1 at Dens Park on August 30, and Tuesday is the second of three league games between the sides before the split.

Bradley Fink and Joe Westley share the Dundee scoring lead with four league goals each, and Westley, who takes the penalties, came off the bench to equalise at St Johnstone within two minutes of the restart.

Hibernian Scottish Premiership form:.

Hibernian form (all competitions):.

Dundee Scottish Premiership form:.

Dundee form (all competitions):.

Passlack, who took the captaincy from Boyle after Reedijk's arrival, is out with a hamstring injury sustained in the eighth minute at Aberdeen, and Reedijk has refused to put a date on his return as the defender races to be fit for the Rangers final.

Alex Williams replaced Passlack at Pittodrie and made his first start against United, so he is the likely right-back again.

Grant Hanley is out after thumb surgery, Adam Mayor has a hamstring problem, and on-loan Stoke City striker Nathan Lowe has a stress fracture that Reedijk will assess week by week.

Kanayo Megwa remains sidelined with a thigh problem and Rocky Bushiri is still recovering from the Achilles injury he suffered in May.

Left-back Jordan Obita is back in contention after a calf injury, and on-loan Manchester United midfielder Jacob Devaney returned from international duty with Ireland, giving Reedijk extra options if he rings the changes.

Owen Elding, 20, leads the line in Lowe's absence, with Boyle and McGrath operating around him as they did in the Hampden semi-final.

For the visitors, Bevan serves the first of a two-match ban after his straight red card against Hearts, ruling him out at Easter Road and at Aberdeen on Saturday, November 28.

Joe Wright, who was on the bench against Hearts, is the natural replacement alongside Ryan Astley, but he has played little league football this season.

Simon Murray, Finlay Robertson and Jack Moorhouse are all out for the season with anterior cruciate ligament injuries.

Bobby Wales, the on-loan striker, is still recovering from an ankle injury.

Goodman, beaten eight times at Dens Park, is expected to keep his place in goal.

Hibernian possible starting lineup:.

Sallinger; Williams, Kerr, Ivezic, Iredale; Chaiwa, Newell; McGrath, Mulligan, Boyle; Elding.

Dundee possible starting lineup:.

Goodman; D. Wright, Astley, J. Wright, Samuels; Forrest, Hamilton, Finnigan, Reilly; Westley, Fink.

Hibernian have not won a league game at Easter Road all season and have shipped 15 goals in seven home matches, and a side that has just lost 4-0 to United at home is unlikely to turn that around in three days against opponents who beat them at Dens Park on August 30.

Dundee arrive without Bevan and with the memory of an 8-0 defeat, and a makeshift centre-back pairing facing Elding and Boyle will struggle to hold a clean sheet.

The counter-argument is that Pittodrie remains Reedijk's only league win, but Dundee's points have come overwhelmingly at Dens Park, and their goal difference of minus five is the worst in the top eight, which is why a Hibernian goal looks likelier than a clean sheet for either side.

Anthropic IPO: four ways the AI giant wants to disrupt science
