💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S.
  • Fossil teeth suggest that Homo erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago.
  • Artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Fossil teeth suggest that Homo erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago. Researchers had thought that these ancient hominins had been limited to savannahs and open woodlands, notes Kira Westaway, a geochronologist and a co-author of two newly introduced studies. “This is a really big deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

Reference: Nature paper 1 & paper 2.

Artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. The firm — now valued at a staggering US$1.5 trillion — has major ambitions in science. It made waves earlier this year when it reported that its model Claude had made several major mathematics breakthroughs. The company also launched their first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research and has revealed looks to “substantially” scale up its work in AI-enabled drug discovery. Pitched as a company that prioritizes AI safety, some researchers question whether an IPO — and the accompanying investor demands — might disrupt some of Anthropic’s safety commitments.

Industry observers note that roughly 180 million people could be carrying a previously unknown type of giant virus in their guts. Researchers found DNA from these ‘egoviruses’ in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people, one of which is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the population. Microbiologists say that egoviruses could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly.

Here in Washington DC, tens of thousands of researchers have gathered for the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting — a showcase for everything from neural implants to memory research.

Sources indicate that but when I asked a panel of leaders at the US National Institutes of Health what in neuroscience remains underappreciated, several pointed to the brain’s relationship with the rest of the body. Nora Volkow, director of the National Institute on Drug Abuse, lamented the lack of research into brain metabolism — a blind spot exposed by the surprising neurological effects of GLP-1 drugs.

It has been revealed that amy Bany Adams, acting director of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, offered a reminder of how much remains to be discovered. Of the glymphatic system, the brain’s waste-clearance network, she mentioned: “We didn’t even know it existed when I was in graduate school.” I’m leaving with a longer list of questions about what else we’ve been overlooking.

Neuroscientists are uncovering how the brain orchestrates a tailored mixture of symptoms in response to either a bacterial or viral infection. Presenting at the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting on 15 November, researchers suggested that the brain decodes the type of pathogen that has invaded, accesses memories of past bouts of illness and can even mobilize immune defences at the sight of a sick person. The unpublished findings challenge the long-held view that neurological responses to infection are a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation.

Artificial-intelligence governance requires more than companies’ oversight of their models — it requires “a system of accountability” that works like a national constitution, argues legal scholar Cindy Skach. Firms should be held legally liable when individuals are affected by AI actions that infringe on their fundamental rights, Skach suggests. She proposes ‘human dignity’ as the most important value for the system to uphold. When a person’s dignity is violated — by an AI-generated deepfake or by a chatbot that treats a distressed user as just another interaction — they could petition a court directly to hold the perpetrator accountable.

It has been revealed that do you find networking a nightmare? Three experts share — in the form of short videos — how to grasp the nettle. They suggest thinking about networking as a professional skill that can be learnt and developed, considering arriving early for events and not worrying about volume. One high-quality connection and follow-up conversation is worth more than 100 business cards, claims public-speaking coach Susie Ashfield.

How Noni Madueke grew into a unique piece at Arsenal amid injury absences

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1138 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Alexis Pereira | 23 Nov 2026 21:02.
  • Noni Madueke’s signing for Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had played a game.
  • It has been revealed that A little more than a year later, the discussion is taking on another dimension.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 23 Nov 2026 21:02.

Noni Madueke’s signing for Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had played a game. Signed from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing, and he had to justify an investment in a player who initially appeared destined to be a back-up.

It has been revealed that A little more than a year later, the discussion is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke received a longer run of opportunities and took the space. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle United, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of that growth.

Mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In his press conference, the boss highlighted the variety the forward has added to the game and his involvement without the ball.

Madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives in one-on-one situations.

That characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In 2024-25, he was one of the Premier League players who progressed the ball towards the box the most and created danger mainly through individual carries. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

‘He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forwards,’ Arteta said. ‘And he is doing it in various ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and much more connection to his game.’.

The numbers help show the scale of the growth. According to FotMob’s Premier League 2026-27 data, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, against 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although Saka has played fewer minutes. The growth also shows in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

Sources indicate that ‘And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball,’ Arteta noted. ‘So I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying that a lot.’.

The development is therefore not about abandoning the dribble, but knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, but now seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

Comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right and move inside, but they do it in different ways. Saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and moves naturally between carries, short passes and crosses. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal’s main attacking tools.

Recent findings suggest that madueke offers more explosion in the first movement and tends to seek one-on-one duels more often. He is more vertical, liking to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When confident, he can disorganise a defence without relying on a long build-up.

Recent findings suggest that the creation data help illustrate the difference. As well as beating Saka for chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob’s numbers, Madueke also demonstrates a higher volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps an advantage in shooting and defensive involvement. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

It has been revealed that that difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka may be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that breaks down the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating individual imbalances.

According to recent reports, the Englishman has also shown he can play on the left, a role he took on when Christos Tzolis was absent. There he must adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can go to the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta’s options and stops the team depending on a single alternative for each side.

According to recent reports, the competition with Saka does not need to be seen as an attempt to remove the starter. Arsenal need more than one player able to decide matches, especially in a long season with the Premier League, Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is beginning to offer arguments to be considered more than simple cover.

One detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

According to recent reports, arteta highlighted the player’s reaction as an example to the rest of the squad. The boss stated Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

‘He went to train and came back a different Noni,’ Arteta explained. ‘He was not willing to accept that situation and showed he was determined. Since then, it has been incredible.’.

The individual work did not start now, however. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has worked for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention on being more decisive in the final third.

The result has shown in the numbers: his average of chances created more than doubled compared with the previous season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate rose from 50 per cent to 55 per cent, while his pass accuracy went from 78 per cent to 87 per cent. In open-play crosses, his success rate jumped from 14 per cent to 33 per cent.

Those numbers help explain why Arteta speaks of a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but has begun to execute other actions better, which could previously limit his influence. The growth combined different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

Gary Neville mentioned he expects Arsenal to ‘canter’ to the Premier League title after Liverpool’s emphatic win over ten-man Manchester United.

Defending champions Arsenal are six points clear at the top of the table despite failing to extend their winning run against Newcastle United in a 2-2 draw.

The blow of failing to win at St James’ Park was substantially softened by the fact virtually all of the teams chasing Arsenal also dropped points.

Second-placed Brighton suffered a shock 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull City while Manchester City’s surprising slump continued as Enzo Maresca’s side could only draw 1-1 at home to Fulham.

The only team in the top-four to win this weekend was Liverpool, who smashed ten-man Manchester United 4-0, but the Reds are still a healthy seven points adrift of Arsenal.

Mikel Arteta ended Arsenal’s 22-year wait for a Premier League trophy last season and eight-time title winner Neville expects the Gunners to retain that crown in a ‘very strange’ domestic campaign.

‘Looking at the Premier League top-six right now, Arsenal are clearly the standout team and are going to win the league at a canter,’ Neville stated on his Sky Sports podcast.

According to recent reports, ‘But the rest of the usual top five or six teams, it’s not been this bad has it for a long time? They’re really struggling.

‘Liverpool were obviously a bit better today but Chelsea are struggling, Tottenham are struggling. Manchester United are struggling, Manchester City look like they’ve fallen off a cliff right now compared to the standards they set under Pep Guardiola.

Recent findings suggest that ‘So it’s a really interesting time where other teams are starting to emerge and it’s becoming a lot more competitive. It’s a very strange league this year.’.

Jamie Carragher also expects the Premier League trophy to be staying in north London despite being encouraged by Liverpool’s win over struggling Manchester United.

‘I still think there’s just an inconsistency with Liverpool game-to-game at the moment,’ the Anfield legend noted. ‘I think they will get better the longer the season goes on and people want there to be a title race.

‘But I think most people in the country would look at Arsenal as a team and say they will probably win the title comfortably.

Are Manchester United in a relegation fight? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/jicPbrP2EU.

‘For me, with Liverpool being my team, I want them to be in a position to be the strongest challenger this season and put themselves in a position that they can then challenge Arsenal next season.’.

While Liverpool climbed back into the top-four by beating Manchester United, the Red Devils sunk to 19th in the Premier League.

United were thrashed in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge after Leny Yoro was sent off inside ten minutes at Anfield.

Despite Manchester United’s dismal position, Neville refused to say his former club were in a relegation battle.

Industry observers note that ‘I don’t believe they are in a relegation fight,’ Neville added. ‘They are second bottom but I do think they will come out of it and start to move up the table.

‘It’s embarrassing really. It’s really desperate and it’s tiring watching them. This is the worst Manchester United have ever been in 53 years.’.

Why Andoni Iraola - NOT Jurgen Klopp - deserves credit for fixing Florian Wirtz, Omar Berrada's Sky appearance has made things worse for Man United and is Cole Palmer at the wrong club? IAN LADYMAN on MY FOOTBALL WEEKEND

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 09:00 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • In what transpired to be a lively Sky TV studio at Anfield, Daniel Sturridge turned in one of his own performances of the season.
  • The former Chelsea and Liverpool striker is proving himself a pundit of real substance and he cut to the heart of one of the more ridiculous notions of the week, namely that a week away with Jurgen Klopp had solved all Florian Wirtz’s problems at a stroke.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 07:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 09:00 EST, 23 November 2026.

In what transpired to be a lively Sky TV studio at Anfield, Daniel Sturridge turned in one of his own performances of the season.

The former Chelsea and Liverpool striker is proving himself a pundit of real substance and he cut to the heart of one of the more ridiculous notions of the week, namely that a week away with Jurgen Klopp had solved all Florian Wirtz’s problems at a stroke.

‘I think we should give credit to Andoni Iraola,’ he said as we all breathed a sigh at the sound of some common sense.

The obsession with Klopp among many people who support and follow Liverpool remains terrifyingly real and the former Anfield manager plays to it.

But to suggest – as many who should know better have done – that Klopp managed to fix Wirtz in four sessions last week is as lazy and ridiculous as it is utterly disrespectful to current Liverpool manager Iraola.

Wirtz had a good couple of games with his national team, for sure. He scored three goals which will have done much for confidence. He was fabulous against Manchester United's ten men.

Florian Wirtz has found his form at just the right time for Liverpool.

Reds boss Andoni Iraola deserves credit for the German's transformation this season.

But anybody who has watched even a small portion of Liverpool’s game this season will have seen a player gradually growing in stature and finally, it seems, adjusting to the largely unique rhythms of the Premier League.

Iraola is a talented coach. Talk to players and staff at Bournemouth and they will tell you that. He improves footballers and steadily he is bringing his influence to bear on Wirtz.

According to recent reports, the 23-year-old still has some way to go. He can still look half a yard too slow on occasion. But he has created 29 Liverpool chances from open play this season.

Klopp can’t take any credit for that.

It tends to be the execs rather than the managers who get the blame at United but Mauricio Pochettino sadly had his fingerprints on what happened on Merseyside.

Industry observers note that he was right to complain about the sending off of Leny Yoro. Alexander Isak was never getting the ball and referee Sam Barrott should have given himself time to consider that before getting the red card out.

In those situations the defender should be given the benefit of any doubt.

The decision has an enormous impact on the game, something that seemed to pass many people by.

Nevertheless the passage of play had at its inception a horror moment from Matthijs de Ligt that most of us could have seen coming the moment the team sheet dropped.

Sometimes it doesn’t pay for a manager to try and be the smartest bloke in the room.

Mauricio Pochettino should shoulder some of the blame for United's dismal defeat at Anfield.

BERRADA INTERVENTION NOT USEFUL FOR UNITED.

No doubt the decision to plonk Omar Berrada in front of a TV camera was driven by good intentions by United.

The club’s executives had been accused of hiding while Old Trafford burned so here was one of them, sitting smartly in front of a huge club crest, ready to tell the world that everything would be OK.

The only problem is that the words of Berrada, United’s chief executive, have arguably made things worse.

Berrada didn’t catch much of a break over the weekend.

Just 48 hours after telling the world that United were happy with their ‘nine defenders’  Pochettino’s team were given such a chasing at Anfield that one wondered if the latest manager may be tempted to chuck all of them on at the same time.

In a recent development, none of this is about luck, however. Neither good nor bad. It’s about planning and the lack thereof.

Liverpool, remember, also had a major defensive problem over the summer.

Omar Berrada's surprise appearance on Sky Sports has made things worse for Man United.

The two full-backs bought in the summer of 2025 – Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez – had struggled while another – Conor Bradley – was injured. In the centre, Ibrahima Konate had left for Real Madrid while young prospect Giovanni Leoni had not played since suffering a dreadful knee injury on his debut last year.

That left Virgil Van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet and Joe Gomez. Liverpool could have struggled on. They could have counted numbers and hoped. They could have prayed for better form and fitness from the defenders they had.

In a recent development, but that would have been unfair on incoming manager Iraola. So in mid-August they took the Uruguayan international Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona and it has transpired to be a signing utterly fundamental to Liverpool’s season so far.

There was little fuss and fanfare about the deal. All the noise was reserved for the £125million winger Bradley Barcola.

Recent findings suggest that but Araujo – signed as a centre-half – is a former Barcelona captain and has solved Liverpool’s right-back problem at a stroke. He was as unfussy and effective against United yesterday as he has been all season.

It has been revealed that this is how recruitment at substantial clubs works. They identify problems and use their data, imagination and contacts to solve them. They don’t count the number of bodies in the dressing room and then sit on their hands telling themselves it is enough.

Every United supporter in the land could have told Berrada and his friends that United needed defensive quality in the summer. But United thought they knew best and were wrong.

It is genuinely terrifying to think just what they may do next.

The second most productive footballer in terms of assists in the league is Brighton’s Pascal Gross but the German was left as bemused as anyone as his team somehow managed to lose a game they dominated at Hull.

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler has said he wants his players to behave like a big team but perhaps some naivety let them down as Hull scored two in added time on Humberside.

The first of Ollie McBurnie’s goals came in the 92nd minute on the back of a quick counter and it was one that could have been stopped at source by what Pep Guardiola used to call a ‘technical foul’ – a trip or a nudge – before the ball had even crossed the halfway line.

Nobody wishes to encourage foul play but the truth is that Guardiola’s City would not have conceded that goal. Nor, for that matter, would Arsenal.

Brighton's naivety saw them suffer a surprise defeat by Hull City on Sunday.

At the Etihad, Enzo Maresca gave Phil Foden a start ahead of Rayan Cherki and the City playmaker revealed some glimpses of his fabulous talent.

Nevertheless the longer this period of uncertainty goes on for Foden, the harder it is to work out how it ends.

Maresca wants to play with two out and out wide players at City.

Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye started in the draw against Fulham while Antoine Semenyo will play when he is fit.

So with Cherki established as City’s creative hub just behind Haaland, Foden is on the fringes a little.

He signed a contract in June and is now tied to the club until 2030. Equally, Foden will be 27 next May and should be approaching his physical and creative peak.

Meanwhile Cole Palmer’s frustrations with life at Chelsea – highlighted in this column earlier this season – have now boiled over with a show of petulance at the end of his team’s Stamford Bridge hammering at the hands of Leeds.

The more this unfolds, the more it feels like Palmer is at the wrong club.

Palmer – for all that he tries to suggest otherwise – is an emotionally complex young athlete. He can be unpredictable and dramatic.

He needs calm around him, not persistent drift.

Cole Palmer's petulance at Stamford Bridge on Saturday has left us asking: Is he at the wrong club?

Another stunning result for Daniel Farke’s Leeds who now sit sixth in the table with the second best defensive record in the top flight.

Farke remains out of contract next summer and that still feels odd.

The club’s favourite media outlets told us last month that an ‘agreement had been reached in principle’ but still no white smoke from Elland Road.

LONG ROAD AHEAD FOR THE UPCOMING KID.

Tottenham have crept into the top half for the first time this season after beating Ipswich with credit due to manager Roberto de Zerbi for handing teenager Luca Williams-Barnett his chance.

With big money summer signings Savio and Omar Marmoush sitting on the bench, Williams-Barnett scored the opening goal and became the fourth youngest player in history to score on his first Premier League start.

Of the three ahead of him in the list, Canadian Daniel Jebbison, now 23, currently sits on the Bournemouth bench, Danny Cadamarteri’s career became rather itinerant once he made the last of his 94 Everton league starts while Mark Cullen travelled from Hull to Bamber Bridge via outposts such as Luton, Blackpool, Port Vale, Hartlepool and Fylde.

Williams-Barnett will have enjoyed his weekend but history tells us the road ahead may not be straight.

Luca Williams-Barnett became the fourth youngest debut goalscorer in Premier League history.

Of the new managers in this season’s top division, it has taken time for some to find their feet.

Iraola now has a statement Anfield win, for example, while at Bournemouth and Fulham Marco Rose and Alvaro Arbeloa no longer have to look at the league table through their fingers.

At Newcastle, it appears rather more complicated.

Eddie Howe’s replacement Matthias Jaissle doesn’t look chuffed with the players he was handed in the summer window but historical concerns stalk him too.

Last season’s big money flop Yoane Wissa started this one well and looked ready to fly after starring and scoring in an August win at Spurs.

That was the £50million forward’s last goal, though, and he also only has one assist to his name.

On Saturday in the gutsy draw with Arsenal he came on in the 83rd minute and that spoke volumes.

One player whose career has headed the other way is Aston Villa defender Victor Lindelof.

The Swede was signed on a free from Manchester United largely to make the numbers up in August 2025 but his rise to prominence has been such that Match of the Day were moved to note his absence through injury from the team that drew with Sunderland at Villa Park.

Lindelof is 32 now but has just signed a latest contract at Villa. Another one to benefit from Unai Emery’s regenerative elixir.

Unai Emery's coaching magic has helped transform the fortunes of Victor Lindelof.

If this weekend has been – in part – about defenders then the Fulham recruitment staff deserve their props too.

The west London club had conceded seven goals in losing their opening three league games before Austrian defender David Affenbruger arrived on the last day of the summer window.

Debuting in the 0-0 draw at Liverpool that followed, Fulham have since lost just one of the seven subsequent games in which he has played.

The fee? £8.5million. Further proof that it really can be done.

Keane Lewis-Potter netted a quickfire brace to put the Bees in control, before their position was strengthened further by James Tarkowski's 40th-minute red card for a challenge that was deemed dangerous after a VAR review.

In the second half, Vitaly Janelt produced a stunning long-range effort, and Fabio Carvalho netted his second league goal of the season to seal back-to-back home wins.

Not only did they claim an impressive victory, but the Bees also hit a notable goalscoring milestone in the process.

Lewis-Potter's deflected opener will go down in history as Brentford's 300th Premier League goal.

The milestone strike took place over five years after Sergio Canos scored Brentford's first Premier League goal in a 2-0 victory over Arsenal.

Yoane Wissa may have damaged his relationship with Brentford supporters with the manner of his exit to Newcastle United in the summer of 2025, but he played a key role in the Bees hitting the 300-goal mark, considering he is the club's leading Premier League goalscorer with 45 goals in 137 games.

Bryan Mbeumo is in second place on Brentford's all-time Premier League goalscorer list with 42 strikes in 136 matches.

Ivan Toney, meanwhile, scored 36 goals in 83 top-flight appearances for the Bees before he left for Al-Ahli in 2024.

Two current Brentford stars, Igor Thiago and Kevin Shade, will be looking to chase the tallies of the aforementioned trio, having scored 24 Premier League goals apiece in their time with the West London club.

Brentford will now turn their focus to three high-profile games against Manchester United, Arsenal and Manchester City.

They will travel to Old Trafford this Saturday with hopes of claiming their first-ever Premier League win over Man United, who are reeling from Sunday's heavy 4-0 loss to Liverpool.

How the Dylan Tombides Foundation is educating footballers about testicular cancer

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that 15 years ago, a random drugs test at the Under-17 World Cup revealed that West Ham striker and Australian youth international Dylan Tombides had testicular cancer. He would pass away three years later at the age of 20.

Originally misdiagnosed by his GP as a cyst, Tombides’ mother, Tracy, and brother, Taylor, are now on a mission to minimise the likelihood of such a mistake happening again by getting people to know what to look for.

Testicular cancer is the most common cancer in males aged 15 to 44, but highly treatable and in most cases curable when detected early - so education is key to saving lives.

That is why the DT38 Foundation was set up in Dylan’s name and why Tracy and Taylor, in partnership with FIFA Medical, are explaining to players at this year’s U17 World Cup in Doha why regular self-examination matters and how to carry it out.

“Getting the call from FIFA was a massive opportunity and an amazing thing for us and for the charity,” Taylor tells Standard Sport.

Industry observers note that “Obviously, it’s where Dylan last kind of played healthy before his diagnosis. So to come back to where it all started for us as a family is a grateful honour.”.

£75m Chelsea star ‘considered retirement’ under Maresca.

Fernandes fumes in unseen interview amid latest Man Utd red card verdict.

Chelsea injury update: Caicedo, Joao Pedro, James latest return dates.

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events.

Tracy and Taylor have spoken to more than 1,200 players across the tournament, and their story has really hit home.

It has been revealed that “One of the young players stood in front of me and remarked, ‘I’m so sorry for your loss. I’m sorry your son isn’t coming home to you. We are so grateful that you are telling us all about it’,” Tracy states.

“(We are) very grateful to have this opportunity to educate 1,200 players out here this fortnight, that hopefully will go home and pass on the message of the signs and symptoms of testicular cancer and the importance of an ultrasound scan.”.

The DT38 foundation have a campaign called ‘Check One Two’, encouraging men to check themselves on the first day of every month.

Dylan’s nickname - ‘Didge’ - also provides an acronym and hashtag for the foundation: Delay Is Deadly, Get Educated.

FIFA medical director Andy Massey has worked with the DT38 Foundation to get Tracy and Taylor talking to players at the U17 World Cup and says it is an initiative that he hopes to continue year on year.

“What I would love to do is carry this on next year for the Under-17s,” Massey indicates.

Industry observers note that “It’s an annual event now (the World Cup) for Under-17s. We’re going to be in the same place until 2029, and it would be fantastic to do it (talk to players) again for next year and the year after.”.

We’re not just affecting one life, we’re affecting a whole generation of lives, which is the biggest part of it.

Massey continued by underlining the value of the work Tracy and Taylor are doing, with free scans now on offer to players during the tournament.

Industry observers note that “We don’t want this to be a box-ticking exercise. We don’t want this to be a, ‘Let’s pat ourselves on the back, we’re working for a charity’.

“This is one of the biggest things that I think I’ve ever done in my sports medicine career because it has such a reach.”.

The DT38 Foundation are starting with the U17 World Cup, but ultimately Taylor hopes their work will have an impact down the generations.

“The effect is lasting,” he says. “If we can teach these kids now, we know the next generation, they’ll teach their kids and they’ll teach their kids and it’ll be continuous.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re not just affecting one life, we’re affecting a whole generation of lives, which is the biggest part of it. Without FIFA, we couldn’t touch as many people as we have.”.

Visit dt38.org to find out more about the DT38 Foundation, Dylan's story and advice and guidance about testicular cancer.

Peter Schmeichel believes simply avoiding relegation should be Mauricio Pochettino’s main ‘target’ at Manchester United this season.

Pochettino took charge of United for the first time away to bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon and it proved a nightmare start for the Argentine, with his side thumped 4-0 at Anfield.

The Red Devils were reduced to ten men in only the tenth minute after Leny Yoro brought down Alexander Isak, and the visitors’ woes were compounded as Dominik Szoboszlai scored with the resulting free-kick.

Man-of-the-match Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s advantage with an audacious finish just three minutes later, before a pair of second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz put the hosts out of sight.

The result ensured United remained firmly in the relegation zone at the end of the weekend’s drama, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

The Old Trafford giants, who now lead Europe’s top five leagues for most goals conceded (34 in all competitions), will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters at Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

Sources indicate that ‘Realistically, can Manchester United just finish tenth or 12th? It would be okay,’ former United goalkeeper Schmeichel stated on Viaplay following the side’s heavy defeat on Merseyside.

Mauricio Pochettino may have left Gary Neville ‘absolutely stunned’ by picking Matthijs de Ligt against Liverpool, but the Manchester United manager notes there was a simple reason for it.

The new Red Devils boss had a tough opening game in charge as he took his side to Anfield and it ended up being a nightmare debut for the Argentine.

Leny Yoro was shown a red card after eight minutes and Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick.

Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz also netted to complete a comfortable 4-0 win for Andoni Iraola’s men.

It has been revealed that manchester United have now picked up just eight points from 11 games and sit 19th in the Premier League table. Every other club in the division has more wins than the one they have managed.

While the Red Devils clearly have many problems, De Ligt has been a focus of criticism after his performance at Anfield.

The Dutch defender has recovered from a long-term injury, but was starting in the Premier League for the first time in nearly a year, having made two Champions League appearances this season.

The 27-year-old looked a long way off Premier League pace as he was run ragged by the Liverpool front line.

Recent findings suggest that asked why he went for De Ligt alongside Yoro over Harry Maguire, who started on the bench but has been playing regularly this season, Pochettino mentioned: ‘He was training, he played in Champions League before the international duty. I think, when we arrived we saw the combination.’.

Gary Neville watched De Ligt play in the defeat to Como in October and was surprised that he was given the nod at Anfield after his performance in Italy.

Roberto De Zerbi has cast doubt on his future, four months into his first full season at Tottenham Hotspur.

After arriving in March, the 47-year-old has presided over a summer window which has seen the likes of Sandro Tonali, Andrew Robertson and Savio touch down in north London.

But De Zerbi, whose contract with Spurs runs until 2031, has admitted doubts over his long-term future in the game.

The Italian told Canal+: “I don’t think I’ll stay in football much longer. Your life revolves around football, but life isn’t just that.

“That time hasn’t come yet. For me, being a coach at this level is already a dream.”.

After enduring a tough start to the 2026/27 Premier League season, Spurs have won four of their last five fixtures, most recently beating Ipswich 2-0.

Before arriving at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, De Zerbi spent time in Ligue 1 with nine-time champions Marseille after leaving Brighton and Hove Albion, but a 5-0 hammering by rivals PSG saw the Italian depart in February of this year.

The Italian joined Spurs shortly thereafter with the club one point away from a first relegation since 1977, and clinched Premier League survival with final-day delight against David Moyes’ Everton.

Currently sat in 10th place, De Zerbi’s Spurs are targeting a weekend victory against relegation-threatened Sunderland to continue a run of good form, but the manager has his eyes set on more.

He stated: “I don’t measure dreams by the titles won, but more by the human impact you have.

According to recent reports, “I always want to stay the same, always look people in the eye. Even when I make mistakes, because I make a lot of them.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goncalo Ramos got his name on the scoresheet in AC Milan’s rout of Frosinone, but he was forced off in the second half.

In a recent development, as Sky (via Calciomercato.com) report, everything seemed great when Milan were dominating Frosinone at San Siro and scoring nearly every time they went forward. However, during the second half, a minor alarm sounded.

Sources indicate that ruben Amorim was forced to replace his Ramos in the 50th minute. The Portuguese striker – who had scored in the first half – was hastily removed from the pitch by the head coach shortly after Ardon Jashari’s goal to make it 3-1.

The reason? The change was made due to a minor muscle problem that the player reported to the bench, even though Ramos himself did not seem happy about the substitution at the time of the change.

The former PSG man informed the bench that he had a small calf problem and – to avoid worsening the problem – Amorim immediately opted for a substitution. Alphadjo Cisse was sent on in his place, and he scored the fourth goal just a few minutes later.

When he was taken off, Ramos indicated a grimace of disapproval towards his bench, miming the ‘wait’ gesture. He then complained that he would have liked to try to stay on the pitch, but some post-match comments cleared things up.

When asked if his calf is ok, he told DAZN: “Yes, yes, everything’s fine, everything’s fine.” Rabiot later revealed the background to the substitution to Sky, admitting that he played a hand in convincing the coach.

“Gonçalo is the first player to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very important player for us, and we have a lot of matches. I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit,” the Frenchman stated.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, Amorim was asked why he felt it was right for Cisse to come on rather than Francesco Camarda, the only other natural centre-forward in the squad.

“We didn’t spend many minutes near the penalty area; he was behind. Today we were 40 metres from the goal, and Cisse was perfect for that. That’s why I didn’t bring on Camarda for Ramos: I needed someone who could run in behind.”.

Emmanuel Emegha has revealed he was robbed on Saturday after Chelsea's 4-1 loss by Leeds.

He put the Blues ahead at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon - his first goal for the club.

'I'm quick, I know how to make runs in behind, and I know that I can be a nightmare for all the defenders. Nobody has seen me yet. When my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

Recent findings suggest that for Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews remarked. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

Bournemouth striker Evanilson has revealed that he is a big fan of Manchester United - sparking rumours that the Brazilian could make the switch to Old Trafford.

Evanilson has been Bournemouth’s talisman this campaign, scoring in six consecutive Premier League as Marco Rose’s side have shot up the table.

The Cherries have now won nine games in a row across all competitions - including a 3-0 dismantling of Manchester United at Old Trafford in October.

Evanilson scored the pick of the goals, firing home from an audacious angle after rounding Senne Lammens.

The former FC Porto man shared that his favourite club in England is Manchester United - sharing a soft spot for the Red Devils with his fellow countryman, exciting winger Rayan.

Evanilson told Globo Esporte: “So I joke around with Rayan. I think that, here in England, of the big clubs, United are the team I like the most. Rayan said the same thing. When I was a kid, I also used to watch United.”.

“When Cristiano Ronaldo played for United, I watched loads of his highlights. And, man, knowing that I’m here playing against them….

Industry observers note that “This is my third season playing against them. I scored last season and I scored this season at Old Trafford.

“It’s a dream, and I tell everyone this in interviews: it was a dream to play at that stadium, and scoring goals is even more vital.

“So it’s a dream I’ve been fulfilling, scoring a goal against United because of how significant the club is.”.

Evanilson believed his strike at Old Trafford was the finest of his career to date.

He continued: “I think it was the most beautiful goal of my career. Because of the importance of the match and the team we were playing against, scoring a goal like that at Old Trafford.”.

“Without a doubt, that was the most beautiful goal of my career, and I was very happy.”.

It has been revealed that “I had a difficult angle there. It was hard to believe, but when I saw the ball going in, it was a moment of enormous happiness.”.

AI is turbocharging cyberattacks — can computer scientists catch up?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1013 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence systems are transforming the way software vulnerabilities are discovered.Credit: Hailshadow/Getty.
  • The disruption of multiple computer systems run by Microsoft, US air traffic control, the bank JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency has renewed concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure.
  • At the same time, researchers have reported artificial intelligence -assisted discovery of security flaws in Java and PHP software, while hackers have used AI tools to target supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial intelligence systems are transforming the way software vulnerabilities are discovered.Credit: Hailshadow/Getty.

The disruption of multiple computer systems run by Microsoft, US air traffic control, the bank JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency has renewed concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure.

At the same time, researchers have reported artificial intelligence -assisted discovery of security flaws in Java and PHP software, while hackers have used AI tools to target supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe.

Sources indicate that although probably unrelated, these incidents highlight a broader transformation in cybersecurity, say researchers. Artificial intelligence is changing how software vulnerabilities are discovered, allowing both attackers and security specialists to examine vast quantities of computer code at unprecedented speed.

“I think vulnerability discovery without AI is basically dead,” states Steven Murdoch, a computer security researcher at University College London. Researchers in the field who don’t use the technology now risk falling behind, he says.

AI can find weaknesses in software much faster than humans can, giving attackers time to exploit vulnerabilities before organizations can fix them. Researchers now want to understand how thoroughly AI can check software for security flaws, and whether it could introduce new weaknesses.

In a recent development, agentic systems help attackers identify security vulnerabilities more rapidly and systematically. While hackers previously had to spend hours inspecting websites and probing software for weaknesses that offered unauthorized access to networks, AI agents use automated tools that can search millions of lines of computer code.

Google has reported that attackers have already used agentic AI to examine software updates, identify the security problems they address, and then find ways to exploit them.

NEWS: Cyberattacks are hitting research institutions — with devastating effects.

NEWS: Cyberattacks are hitting research institutions — with devastating effects.

Sources indicate that “For me, it's about the scale,” claims Daniel Gardham, a cybersecurity researcher at the University of Surrey. AI tends to find the same kinds of weaknesses as human hackers, but it makes it easier for people with limited technical expertise to break into systems.

“They can set an AI agent off and come back in 20 minutes and have dozens of results already,” he states.

Sources indicate that even with AI, most security breaches still involve human failure, he says, such as weak passwords (a common problem with Europe’s supermarket freezers was that passwords were defaults such as ‘admin’ or ‘12345’) or clicking on links from unfamiliar sources. AI-crafted messages can make such phishing messages more convincing and so more likely to succeed. They can draw on publicly available information to personalize fraudulent communications and make them appear authentic.

Recent findings suggest that murdoch indicates AI is particularly good at discovering familiar kinds of software flaws, even if the most accomplished human researchers remain better at finding entirely latest types of weakness. “They don't need to sleep,” he says. “You can happily work a hundred of them in parallel.”.

These capabilities of AI helped discover security flaws in Java and PHP software, two programming languages that build cross-platform software and websites. In the Java case, for example, AI identified circumstances that could allow an attacker to corrupt computer memory. But Murdoch says the significance of the issue has been exaggerated.

The Java vulnerability, he indicates: “Is a real problem, but it’s not one of the top ten vulnerabilities this year or probably even this week.”.

Just like hackers, cybersecurity researchers are using AI tools to swiftly and efficiently find weaknesses in computer systems. Murdoch states this has become increasingly crucial to vulnerability researchers, who can now examine much larger quantities of software and work out how to patch up the defences where necessary. Researchers are also developing AI agents that can detect and repair vulnerabilities automatically.

When security researchers uncover a weakness, they typically notify the software developer privately, allowing engineers to prepare a remedy before publishing details of the problem.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare.

Murdoch notes the use of AI in cyber security has shortened the time window between public disclosure and attempted exploitation – from several weeks, to just a few days.

It has been revealed that rushing an revision can bring its own problems. A software patch can interfere with other programs and cause the sort of outage that organisations are trying to avoid.

“The life for the defenders who are trying to fix things has become significantly harder,” Murdoch claims.

It’s unlikely that the recent tech outages were connected as large-scale cyber-attack, indicates Murdoch. The most prominent disruptions, he says, are likely technical malfunctions rather than anything more sinister.

Mauricio Pochettino hauled his beleaguered Man United stars back into Carrington early on Monday morning after the new manager's chastening Anfield bow on Sunday.

Pochettino, who replaced Michael Carrick last week, was served a sobering reality check at the hands of United's fierce rivals Liverpool, with the Red Devils on the receiving end of a 4-0 trouncing on Merseyside.

The Argentine bemoaned the impact of what he described as a harsh red card against defender Leny Yoro in the opening eight minutes of the contest, but admitted he has plenty to do to turn things around - with United stuck in 19th in the Premier League table.

And Pochettino had his players check in for training early on Monday morning, with a downcast Bruno Fernandes and his team-mates spotted arriving at around 8.30am - roughly an hour earlier than under Carrick.

Under Carrick's stewardship, players were given the day after a game off, and it remains to be seen whether Pochettino will do away with that approach in favour of a recovery day at the club's training ground - a similar approach to that taken by former United boss Ruben Amorim.

Man United stars were ordered back into training on Monday after their trouncing at Anfield.

Matthijs de Ligt cut a contemplative figure as he drove through the gates at Carrington.

Director of football Jason Wilcox continues to have questions to answer after Man United were unable to elevate themselves out of the relegation zone.

News also came on Monday that Man United are appealing to the FA over Yoro’s controversial red card.

According to recent reports, yoro was sent off in the eighth minute for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free kick as 10-man United were thrashed 4-0.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

In September, Pro Ref boss Howard Webb apologised to United when Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand after VAR incorrectly ruled that teammate Enzo Fernandez was not interfering with play as he tried to head the ball in an offside position.

Last season, Webb acknowledged that the match officials got it wrong when they decided not to send off Brentford captain Nathan Collins for hauling back Bryan Mbeumo inside the box as United lost 3-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Newly introduced United head coach Pochettino blamed Yoro’s red card for the heavy defeat in his first game in charge, and was unhappy that Barrott took no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty area moments earlier.

In a recent development, 'So painful, so disappointed,' stated the Argentine. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

'It's clear that after eight minutes the strategy was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

Recent findings suggest that 'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

It has been revealed that 'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

According to recent reports, 'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'.

But more critical were former Red Devils Roy Keane and Gary Neville, both of whom were pushed to extremes assessing the match after the final whistle.

Lisandro Martinez was among the Man United defenders that Gary Neville did not feel were up to the task at Anfield.

But incoming manager Pochettino was keen to place the majority of blame on the harsh red card doled out to Leny Yoro.

Neville was driven to slapping his face in the Sky Sports studio to demonstrate Man United's defenders' lack of hunger and poise.

'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', he stated before pointing to his head.

'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'.

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'.

The Overlap broadcaster slapped himself a number of times while repeating 'wake up!' and adding: 'You play for Man United'.

Keane was pushed to the brink of swearing in his snap description of the team's performance, adding that he thought Neville's verdict - that the 4-0 scoreline might have been worse under the circumstances - took players off the hook.

'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane said immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

According to recent reports, 'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'.

Industry observers note that '(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

In a recent development, 'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

Recent findings suggest that 'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

Sources indicate that 'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

Tottenham have been linked to Piero Ausilio, with the former Inter Milan sporting director earmarked for a similar role at the Premier League club.

Italian outlet Tuttosport report that Spurs are closing in on a deal to bring Ausilio to north London.

It is hoped that Ausilio could be installed in time to take charge of Spurs’ transfer approach for the January transfer window.

Tottenham’s executive structure has frequently changed since 2023.

Fabio Paratici joined the club in 2021 as sporting director, but stepped down in April 2023 ahead of a 30-month ban from all football activities handed to him by FIFA after a conviction for financial malpractice.

Paratici returned to his role in October 2025 after the conclusion of his suspension, sharing duties with co-sporting director Johan Lange.

But his return did not last long, as Paratici quit Spurs in February of this year, meaning Lange stepped up to become sole sporting director.

Ausilio ended a 28-year association with Inter Milan in the summer, with the Italian giants deciding not to renew his contract as sporting director.

Initially joining the club’s youth academy in 1998, Ausilio worked his way through the ranks to become sporting director in 2014.

Midway through his first season in his role, Ausilio was named as the TMW award’s best sporting director at the start of 2015. In 2024 Ausilio was recognised as the ‘best sporting director’ in football at the Globe Soccer Awards.

Retiring from football after injury as a teenager, Ausilio holds a degree in law, having studied at the University of Milan.

Over the years Ausilio has garnered a strong reputation for his scouting and squad-building, helping to construct a team at the San Siro that has won three Serie A titles and reached the Champions League final twice in the past five seasons.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.

Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.

A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, showed the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.

Sources indicate that ‘To all the idiots on my Snapchat, that is a solar eclipse! In France, all they got was a little croissant from the bakery,’ Pepe joked at the time.

Unsurprisingly, the wild rumour promptly spread online amongst fans, many of whom mocked Pepe for apparently going against the advice of experts and wilfully exposing himself to intense visible light, ultraviolet and infrared radiation.

But on Sunday evening, Pepe’s club Villarreal released a statement vehemently denying these baseless claims on social media.

‘Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to observing the solar eclipse,’ the statement from the La Liga outfit read.

Villarreal confirmed that Pepe had indeed undergone surgery but stressed that it was ‘entirely unrelated’ to the solar eclipse.

‘The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event,’ the statement continued.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health.’.

The surgery Pepe underwent meant the ex-Arsenal attacker was sidelined for Villarreal’s games against Real Madrid, Napoli, Elche, Liverpool and Valencia last month.

The Ivory Coast international made his return in Villarreal’s Copa del Rey first-round tie with Manacor, in which he scored his side’s final goal in a thumping 5-0 victory.

He has gone on to feature in all of Villarreal’s next four matches, although he has failed to complete 90 minutes in any of those contests.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since joining Villarreal from Trabzonspor back in 2024, Pepe has made a total of 86 appearances for the Spanish club, chipping in with 14 goals and 18 assists in that time.

Villarreal surrendered an early two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday and sit tenth in La Liga after 13 matches.

Pepe became Arsenal’s club-record signing when he signed from Lille for a fee of £72million back in 2019 – and the move remains the third most expensive deal in the Gunners’ history, behind those involving Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes.

Despite enjoying an encouraging start, Pepe badly struggled to live up to expectations at the Emirates and has often been branded one of the worst signings of the Premier League era.

"It's not that they surprised me; I knew they were very good. But honestly I've enjoyed analysing them," Iraola said about Brugge.

Industry observers note that "I think we will have to be at a very, very good level, otherwise it is going to be very difficult. They have players who can make the difference, and obviously we also have.

According to recent reports, “It’s a result that definitely needs to be managed, navigated, and channeled, but it doesn’t change my attitude at all. We have 20 points today. By Ben Sully | 24 Nov 2026 00:47, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 03:23.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher has claimed Chelsea have "no chance of achieving anything" under Xabi Alonso unless they sign a physical centre-back.

Alonso has made an underwhelming start to his time at Stamford Bridge, having overseen five wins, one draw and five losses in the Premier League.

Chelsea's frailties in the defensive third have contributed to their inconsistency, having shipped 20 goals in 11 league games this term, leaving them with the fifth-worst defensive record in the top flight.

The Blues shipped four of those goals in Saturday's demoralising 4-1 defeat against Leeds United at Stamford Bridge.

Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill started as Chelsea's centre-back pairing at the weekend, with Maxence Lacroix currently sidelined with a hamstring injury.

Speaking on Sky Sports' Monday Night Football, Carragher criticised Fofana and Colwill for their lack of physicality, telling Chelsea to address the centre-back position in the January transfer window.

"Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back, and if they don't change it in January, they're going to have a significant problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League," Carragher mentioned.

"Colwill at Sunderland against Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half-time.

"Fofana's performance against Man United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you'll see from a centre-back this season.

"As a partnership, this will never work because they're not physical enough and there's no real leader there.

"It almost feels like you've got two novices playing, but one cost £75m, and Colwill has been talked up a lot not just at Chelsea but at international level as well.".

It has been revealed that "Those two can't play in a back four as a two, but it reminds me of myself at Liverpool. We didn't fix it defensively and we were seen as weak, conceding from set pieces and long throws.

"It wasn't until we signed Sami Hyypia, 6ft 4in, dominant centre-back, leader, great player, that it changed for us.

"This is not going to change with what they have. Lacroix is a decent player, that's a sticking plaster until the next transfer window in January or the end of the season.

"Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they've got absolutely no chance of achieving anything.".

After splashing out £52m on Lacroix in the summer, Chelsea may be somewhat reluctant to spend more money on their central defence in the January window.

However, if their defensive complications persist, they may be forced into recruiting a newly introduced centre-back in a bid to add some much-needed solidity to Alonso's backline.

Recently, Chelsea have been mentioned as a potential suitor for AC Milan defender Koni De Winter, who has also been linked with Manchester United and Liverpool.

Chelsea are also said to be interested in Lens defender Pierre Ismael Ganiou, who has drawn comparisons with former Real Madrid centre-back Raphael Varane.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he rolled out into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he said, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk.

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’.

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that it should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

Industry observers note that ‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he stated. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

Sources indicate that ‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

Industry observers note that ‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

Sources indicate that he added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’.

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

Published: 05:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:57 EST, 23 November 2026.

Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon just two days after attempting to confront angry fans following defeat to Newport on Saturday.

The journeyman manager had himself called the 2-0 loss on the road 'unforgivable' after he was taunted by home supporters chanting that he would be 'sacked in the morning' after the result.

Holloway had intended to go down the tunnel after the final whistle, and passed the away stand on his route out, taking off his cap as he held up his hands in resignation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women’s Super League strugglers Crystal Palace have been handed a three-point deduction after breaching substitution rules against Everton in September.

Palace opened their WSL campaign with a 1-0 victory over the Toffees thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith’s first-half goal.

But they will not be able to keep hold of their points haul from that victory, having made use of a fourth substitution window in second-half injury time, when only three are permitted per match.

That saw them introduce Kirsty Howat in place of Shannon O’Brien in the seventh of eight added minutes.

A statement from the WSL confirms Crystal Palace admitted their breach of competition rules, while an independent tribunal dubbed the move “inadvertent” and “not intended to secure an unfair advantage”. It also acknowledged Palace have taken steps to ensure the incident would not be repeated.

However, it maintained a sporting sanction would be necessary, writing: “The integrity of the competition would be damaged if a club that had breached the rules on substitution opportunities, and had won the match, were allowed to keep the points it obtained.”.

Howat did not touch the ball in her time on the pitch, which lasted less than one minute, though Everton maintained her introduction handed the Eagles an unfair advantage. The tribunal concurred, adding in their decision that Howat’s lack of influence on the match did not amount to “exceptional circumstances.”.

It has been revealed that the imposed three-point deduction will leave Palace on six points with 11 matches played and drop them to 11th place in the table, above only winless Charlton Athletic. Should they finish the season in that position, they would face a play-off with the WSL2’s second-place finisher for their place in the top flight.

Palace stated in a club statement that they are “disappointed” by the tribunal’s decision, adding they feel they have been stripped of a “deserved victory.”.

The statement read: “Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty – a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.”.

Palace do not have the option to appeal the tribunal’s decision.

The 34-year-old appears to be under minimal pressure from his current deputy, Giorgi Mamardashvili, who may have to assess his own future if it becomes clear there is no clear path to being Liverpool's number one.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Senegal have been confirmed as champions of AFCON 2025 after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld their appeal, bringing an end to an ugly months-long saga.
  • Morocco and Senegal met in the AFCON 2025 final, but the match was beset by unprecedented controversy.
  • Late in regular time, Morocco were awarded a penalty, which Senegal protested by leaving the pitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Senegal have been confirmed as champions of AFCON 2025 after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld their appeal, bringing an end to an ugly months-long saga.

Morocco and Senegal met in the AFCON 2025 final, but the match was beset by unprecedented controversy.

Late in regular time, Morocco were awarded a penalty, which Senegal protested by leaving the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that players and staff, led by head coach Pape Thiaw, alike returned to the changing rooms, and the match was paused for 14 minutes. Some Senegal players remained on the pitch and returned to the pitch only at the behest of captain Sadio Mane.

Crucially, the referee never abandoned the match, and play resumed once the entire Senegal squad had returned to the pitch.

Brahim Diaz then missed the vital penalty and Senegal went on to win in extra time, with Villarreal’s Pape Gueye scoring the decider.

In a recent development, in March 2026, two months after the final, CAF confirmed the shock decision to reverse the result, saying Senegal had forfeited the match by leaving the pitch. The result was thus changed to a 3-0 win for Morocco.

Senegal then appealed the decision at CAS, and have now been reinstated as champions after it was confirmed their appeal was upheld.

A statement from CAS read: “The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025). The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated.

“Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).”.

A decision shared in a press release on Tuesday explained: “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

“In the panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.”.

The panel decided that Articles 82 and 84 of the tournament rules, which formed the basis of Morocco’s appeal, were only applicable when a referee was forced to permanently call off a match. Given he allowed the match to restart and finish, those articles were no longer considered applicable.

“In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law,” the court press release continued.

“The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as ‘arbitrary’. On the contrary, the referee’s judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
